name: c-rust-dust-wasteland
prompt: A tall vertical 9:16 oil painting, an extreme wide view from far back and slightly above, of what used to be a city park, long after everything has already happened. The ground is cracked, drifted ochre dirt running to a low horizon; iron railings rusted to the colour of dried blood lean and fold into the dust; a single leafless tree stands black and split; a toppled street lamp lies half buried, its glass gone, its column crumbling into grey ash. The air itself is thick with suspended grit, so distant shapes dissolve into a brown haze. The light is a sourceless, flat midday glare filtered through dust, no shadows worth the name, the sun only a dull smear. The whole canvas keeps to a narrow, related palette of ochre, burnt sienna, rust and umber, painted densely with fine, obsessive texture: grain, flaking crusts, fibrous dust on every surface, the brushwork patient and meticulous rather than loose. At the exact centre, tiny in the vastness, a park bench stands untouched and whole, and on it sits a fat gentleman in a black top hat and a spotless black frock coat with a white shirtfront, plump and pink-cheeked, perfectly groomed, not a speck of dust on him, the only clean, cool, crisp thing in the picture. He sits relaxed, legs crossed, one gloved hand lifted in a lazy dismissive wave at the empty seat beside him and the empty land beyond, a small satisfied smile; there is no one there to wave at. The upper third is open, featureless dust-brown sky, empty for a caption. No text, letters, words or signage anywhere in the image. Thanks.
